title: Cube Crate

serves.summary: The learner packs a crate with unit cubes layer by layer and finds its volume, finds a volume from one layer and the height, and builds crates of a given volume, including one twice as big (doubling one edge, not all three), which shows volume as length × width × height.

request.objective: Measure the volume of a rectangular prism by packing it with unit cubes layer by layer, relate it to length × width × height, and reason about how changing one edge changes the volume (5.MD.C.3-5).

problems.ask: Pack the crate with cubes. What is its volume?
problems.goal: The sign says 12 cubic units: a layer of 6, two layers.

problems.ask: There are only enough cubes for one layer. What is the volume of the crate?
problems.goal: The sign says 36: a layer of 12 cubes fits 3 times up the crate.

problems.ask: Make a crate 2 cubes tall that holds exactly 24 cubes.
problems.goal: Length × width = 12 with height 2 (4 by 3, 6 by 2 or 3 by 4).

problems.ask: Make a crate that holds exactly twice as many cubes as the grey crate.
problems.goal: Any crate of 24 cubes, e.g. doubling one edge only (2 by 2 by 6).
